1 وَمِدَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ , (S, L, K.) aor. تَوْمَدُ, inf. n. وَمَدٌ, (L,) The night was, or became, one of وَمَد, i. e., intense heat, &c., as explained below. (S, L, K. *) One also says وَمِدَ اليَوْمُ: but the former is more common. (M, L.) ―
-b2- وَمِدَ عَلَيْهِ, (S, * M, A, L, K *,) aor. يَوْمَدُ, (K,) inf. n. وَمَدٌ, (M, L, K;) (tropical:) He was angry with him; (S, M, A, L, K;) was incensed against him; i. q. وَبِدَ, (S, L,) of which it is a dial. form. (S.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
